06-01.title: Marilyn Monroe
06-01.description: The most iconic Hollywood actress and sex symbol of the 20th century, whose luminous performances in Some Like It Hot and Gentlemen Prefer Blondes made her a cultural legend.

06-01.title: Morgan Freeman
06-01.description: Oscar-winning American actor whose resonant voice and commanding presence in films like The Shawshank Redemption and Million Dollar Baby define screen gravitas.

06-01.title: Andy Griffith
06-01.description: Beloved American actor and comedian who charmed generations as the folksy Sheriff Andy Taylor on The Andy Griffith Show for eight iconic seasons.

06-01.title: CNN Launches
06-01.description: Ted Turner launched CNN as the world's first 24-hour cable news network, forever transforming how people consume news around the globe.

06-01.title: Adolf Eichmann Executed
06-01.description: Nazi SS officer Adolf Eichmann was hanged in Israel after being convicted of crimes against humanity for his central role in organizing the Holocaust.

06-01.title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band — The Beatles
06-01.description: The Beatles released their psychedelic masterpiece, widely considered the greatest rock album ever made, unleashing a studio revolution that defined the Summer of Love.

06-01.title: Rope
06-01.description: Alfred Hitchcock's claustrophobic thriller, filmed in a single apartment in apparent real-time, starred James Stewart and pushed the boundaries of cinematic tension.

06-02.title: Thomas Hardy
06-02.description: Victorian novelist and poet who immortalized the English countryside in sweeping tragedies like Tess of the d'Urbervilles and Far from the Madding Crowd.

06-02.title: Charlie Watts
06-02.description: The meticulously restrained drummer of the Rolling Stones who anchored the world's greatest rock and roll band with jazz-inflected precision for nearly six decades.

06-02.title: Pete Conrad
06-02.description: NASA astronaut and the third person to walk on the Moon during Apollo 12, known for his irreverent humor and the famous quip upon landing on the lunar surface.

06-02.title: Coronation of Queen Elizabeth II
06-02.description: Queen Elizabeth II was crowned at Westminster Abbey in the first British coronation to be televised, watched by 27 million people across the United Kingdom.

06-02.title: PLO Founded
06-02.description: The Palestine Liberation Organization was established in Cairo to represent the Palestinian people, becoming one of the most significant political bodies in the Middle East.

06-02.title: The Eminem Show — Eminem
06-02.description: Eminem's fourth studio album debuted at number one on both UK and US charts, cementing his reign as hip-hop's most provocative and commercially dominant voice.

06-02.title: Italian Job
06-02.description: This quintessential British caper film starring Michael Caine as a slick gold-heist mastermind became a beloved classic, famous for its Mini Cooper car-chase finale.

06-03.title: Allen Ginsberg
06-03.description: Beat Generation poet whose raw and ecstatic masterpiece Howl shattered literary convention and became the defining cry of the counterculture movement.

06-03.title: Josephine Baker
06-03.description: American-born French entertainer, civil rights activist, and resistance spy who dazzled Paris in the 1920s and became the first Black woman to star in a major film.

06-03.title: Tony Curtis
06-03.description: Charismatic Hollywood star who delivered career-defining performances in Some Like It Hot and The Defiant Ones, earning an Academy Award nomination for the latter.

06-03.title: Ed White First American Spacewalk
06-03.description: Astronaut Edward White floated outside the Gemini IV capsule for 23 minutes, becoming the first American to walk in space and describing the experience as the saddest moment of his life when it ended.

06-03.title: Tiananmen Square Massacre
06-03.description: Chinese military forces violently suppressed pro-democracy protesters in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, with the iconic image of a lone man facing a tank becoming a symbol of resistance worldwide.

06-03.title: Stadium Arcadium — Red Hot Chili Peppers
06-03.description: The Red Hot Chili Peppers released their sprawling double album to instant chart domination in both the US and UK, featuring the hit singles Snow and Dani California.

06-03.title: Cléo from 5 to 7
06-03.description: Agnès Varda's groundbreaking French New Wave film follows a pop singer wandering Paris in real time while awaiting cancer test results, a feminist masterwork ahead of its era.

06-04.title: Angelina Jolie
06-04.description: Oscar-winning actress and humanitarian who captivated audiences in Girl, Interrupted and Maleficent while becoming one of the world's most prominent philanthropists.

06-04.title: George III
06-04.description: King of Great Britain whose long reign witnessed both the American Revolution and the Napoleonic Wars, and who suffered from a mysterious mental illness that gripped the nation.

06-04.title: Noah Wyle
06-04.description: American actor who became a household face as the compassionate Dr. John Carter across fifteen years of the medical drama ER.

06-04.title: Dunkirk Evacuation Ends
06-04.description: Operation Dynamo concluded with over 338,000 Allied troops rescued from the beaches of Dunkirk as Winston Churchill delivered his immortal 'We shall fight on the beaches' speech.

06-04.title: First Hot Air Balloon Demonstration
06-04.description: The Montgolfier brothers publicly demonstrated their revolutionary hot air balloon invention in Annonay, France, ushering in the age of human flight.

06-04.title: Born in the U.S.A. — Bruce Springsteen
06-04.description: Springsteen released his career-defining album whose hard-rocking anthems masked biting social commentary, spawning seven Top 10 singles and selling 15 million copies in the US.

06-04.title: Grease
06-04.description: This electrifying musical starring John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John became the highest-grossing film of 1978, with its soundtrack producing some of the most beloved pop songs of the decade.

06-05.title: John Maynard Keynes
06-05.description: British economist whose revolutionary theories on government spending during economic downturns reshaped modern capitalism and gave birth to macroeconomics.

06-05.title: Mark Wahlberg
06-05.description: Boston-born actor and producer who rose from rapper Marky Mark to Oscar-nominated Hollywood star in films like The Departed and Boogie Nights.

06-05.title: Martha Argerich
06-05.description: Argentine classical pianist widely regarded as one of the greatest pianists in history, whose electrifying interpretations of Chopin and Prokofiev are considered definitive.

06-05.title: Six-Day War Begins
06-05.description: Israel launched a devastating pre-emptive strike against Egypt, Jordan, and Syria, and in just six days tripled its territory in one of the most decisive military campaigns of the 20th century.

06-05.title: Robert F. Kennedy Assassinated
06-05.description: Senator Robert F. Kennedy was shot at the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles moments after winning the California presidential primary, robbing a generation of its most hopeful political leader.

06-05.title: Around the World in a Day — Prince
06-05.description: Prince's psychedelic follow-up to Purple Rain debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, showcasing his fearless artistic evolution with the dreamy hit single Raspberry Beret.

06-05.title: The Silence of the Lambs
06-05.description: Jonathan Demme's chilling psychological thriller starring Jodie Foster and Anthony Hopkins became only the third film ever to win all five major Academy Awards.

06-06.title: Prince
06-06.description: Minneapolis musical genius who played virtually every instrument on his recordings and fused funk, rock, and soul into an unclassifiable sound that produced Purple Rain and Sign o' the Times.

06-06.title: Nathan Hale
06-06.description: American patriot and Continental Army spy captured by the British during the Revolutionary War, remembered for his reported last words: 'I only regret that I have but one life to lose for my country.'

06-06.title: Robert Englund
06-06.description: American actor who became a horror icon through his menacing portrayal of the razor-gloved killer Freddy Krueger across the Nightmare on Elm Street franchise.

06-06.title: D-Day: Allied Invasion of Normandy
06-06.description: Operation Overlord launched the largest seaborne invasion in history as 156,000 Allied troops stormed five beaches on the coast of Normandy, turning the tide of World War II.

06-06.title: Tetris Released
06-06.description: Soviet engineer Alexey Pajitnov released the block-stacking puzzle game Tetris, which would go on to become one of the best-selling video games of all time.

06-06.title: It's Dark and Hell Is Hot — DMX
06-06.description: DMX's ferocious debut album stormed to number one in America, establishing the gravelly-voiced Yonkers rapper as one of hip-hop's most commanding forces.

06-06.title: The Omen
06-06.description: Richard Donner's supremely unsettling horror film about the Antichrist disguised as an ambassador's son became one of the defining supernatural thrillers of the 1970s.

06-07.title: Dean Martin
06-07.description: The effortlessly charming Italian-American entertainer whose velvet baritone and tuxedoed cool made him the quintessential Rat Pack showman and one of the best-selling artists of all time.

06-07.title: Liam Neeson
06-07.description: Northern Irish actor who became a global action star following his searing performance as Oskar Schindler in Schindler's List and reinvented himself as the ultimate thriller hero in Taken.

06-07.title: Tom Jones
06-07.description: Welsh singing legend whose powerhouse voice made It's Not Unusual a worldwide hit in 1965, launching one of the most enduring and versatile careers in popular music.

06-07.title: Vatican City Becomes Sovereign State
06-07.description: The Lateran Treaty was ratified, establishing Vatican City as an independent sovereign state and settling decades of conflict between the Holy See and the Italian government.

06-07.title: Lee Resolution Introduced
06-07.description: Richard Henry Lee presented his historic resolution to the Continental Congress declaring the American colonies free and independent states, setting in motion the formal break with Britain.

06-07.title: Transformer — Lou Reed
06-07.description: Produced by David Bowie, Lou Reed's glam-rock breakthrough gave the world Walk on the Wild Side and cemented Reed as the poet laureate of New York's underground.

06-07.title: Ocean's Eleven
06-07.description: Steven Soderbergh's impossibly cool Las Vegas heist film assembled the most glamorous ensemble cast of its era, with George Clooney, Brad Pitt, and Matt Damon effortlessly stealing the show.

06-08.title: Frank Lloyd Wright
06-08.description: America's greatest architect, whose organic designs for Fallingwater and the Guggenheim Museum merged buildings with their natural surroundings in ways never seen before.

06-08.title: Kanye West
06-08.description: Visionary Chicago rapper and producer who revolutionized hip-hop with soul-sampled beats on The College Dropout before pushing boundaries even further with 808s and My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy.

06-08.title: Francis Crick
06-08.description: British molecular biologist who co-discovered the double helix structure of DNA with James Watson in 1953, one of the most important scientific breakthroughs in history.

06-08.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four Published
06-08.description: George Orwell published his prophetic dystopian novel introducing Big Brother, doublethink, and Newspeak to the world — a book that remains essential reading decades later.

06-08.title: Michelangelo's David Installed
06-08.description: Michelangelo's towering marble David was installed in the Piazza della Signoria in Florence, a three-year carving project that became the Renaissance's supreme statement on human perfection.

06-08.title: Sticky Fingers — The Rolling Stones
06-08.description: The Rolling Stones released their first album on their own label, featuring Brown Sugar and Wild Horses, with Andy Warhol's provocative zipper-fly cover artwork shocking and delighting in equal measure.

06-08.title: Ghostbusters
06-08.description: Ivan Reitman's supernatural comedy starring Bill Murray, Dan Aykroyd, and Harold Ramis became a pop culture phenomenon, with Ray Parker Jr.'s theme becoming one of the decade's most inescapable songs.

06-09.title: Peter the Great
06-09.description: Russian Tsar who dragged his nation into the modern era by force of will, building St. Petersburg from scratch and modernizing the Russian military, government, and culture.

06-09.title: Cole Porter
06-09.description: American composer and lyricist whose sophisticated, witty songs for stage and screen — Night and Day, I've Got You Under My Skin — defined the glamour of the Great American Songbook.

06-09.title: Michael J. Fox
06-09.description: Canadian-American actor who became a global superstar as Marty McFly in the Back to the Future trilogy and later became a powerful advocate for Parkinson's disease research.

06-09.title: Emperor Nero Dies
06-09.description: Roman Emperor Nero, facing a coup and military revolt, fled Rome and died by suicide, ending the Julio-Claudian dynasty and plunging Rome into the chaotic Year of the Four Emperors.

06-09.title: Donald Duck Debuts
06-09.description: Walt Disney introduced Donald Duck in the animated short The Wise Little Hen, and the irascible, sailor-suited duck quickly became one of the world's most recognizable cartoon characters.

06-09.title: Confessions on a Dance Floor — Madonna
06-09.description: Madonna's disco-revival masterpiece debuted at number one in more than 40 countries, spawning the smash hit Hung Up and proving she remained pop music's ultimate reinvention artist.

06-09.title: Johnny English
06-09.description: Rowan Atkinson reprised his gift for physical comedy in this gleefully silly spy parody that became an unexpected global box office hit.

06-10.title: Judy Garland
06-10.description: The beloved star of The Wizard of Oz and one of the most celebrated entertainers of the 20th century, whose over-the-rainbow voice moved audiences to tears for generations.

06-10.title: Lin-Manuel Miranda
06-10.description: Puerto Rican-American playwright and composer who revolutionized Broadway with Hamilton, a hip-hop retelling of the Founding Fathers that won 11 Tony Awards.

06-10.title: Prince Philip
06-10.description: Duke of Edinburgh and husband of Queen Elizabeth II for 73 years, whose naval heroism in World War II and decades of royal service made him one of Britain's longest-serving consorts.

06-10.title: Benjamin Franklin's Kite Experiment
06-10.description: Benjamin Franklin flew a kite in a thunderstorm and proved that lightning is electricity, a discovery that led to his invention of the lightning rod and transformed our understanding of nature.

06-10.title: Alcoholics Anonymous Founded
06-10.description: Bill Wilson and Dr. Robert Smith founded Alcoholics Anonymous in Akron, Ohio, creating a twelve-step fellowship that would help millions of people worldwide overcome addiction.

06-10.title: The Marshall Mathers LP — Eminem
06-10.description: Eminem's third album, featuring the era-defining Stan and The Real Slim Shady, rocketed to number one in the US and became one of the fastest-selling rap albums in history.

06-10.title: The A-Team
06-10.description: Joe Carnahan's explosive big-screen adaptation of the classic TV series rebooted the team of elite ex-Special Forces soldiers in a slick, relentlessly entertaining summer blockbuster.

06-11.title: Gene Wilder
06-11.description: American actor and comedian whose manic brilliance as Willy Wonka in the 1971 film and as the terrified sheriff in Blazing Saddles made him one of Hollywood's most beloved comic talents.

06-11.title: Joe Montana
06-11.description: NFL quarterback legend who led the San Francisco 49ers to four Super Bowl victories without throwing a single interception in any of those games, earning the nickname Joe Cool.

06-11.title: Vince Lombardi
06-11.description: Green Bay Packers head coach who never had a losing season and won the first two Super Bowls, leaving behind a legacy of discipline and excellence so profound the Super Bowl trophy bears his name.

06-11.title: Henry VIII Marries Catherine of Aragon
06-11.description: Henry VIII wed Catherine of Aragon in a marriage that would ultimately fracture the English Church from Rome when the Pope refused to grant an annulment, sparking the English Reformation.

06-11.title: FIFA World Cup Opens in South Africa
06-11.description: The first FIFA World Cup held on African soil kicked off in Johannesburg, South Africa, with the haunting sound of the vuvuzela becoming one of the tournament's most memorable features.

06-11.title: Debut — Björk
06-11.description: Björk's explosive solo debut fused dance music, jazz, and orchestral arrangements into an otherworldly sound that announced one of the most original artistic voices of the decade.

06-11.title: Jurassic Park
06-11.description: Steven Spielberg's dinosaur blockbuster used then-revolutionary CGI to bring prehistoric creatures terrifyingly to life, becoming the highest-grossing film in history at the time of its release.

06-12.title: George H. W. Bush
06-12.description: The 41st President of the United States, a decorated World War II naval pilot who guided the nation through the fall of the Berlin Wall and the first Gulf War.

06-12.title: Anne Frank
06-12.description: German-born Jewish diarist whose account of hiding from the Nazis in a secret Amsterdam annex became one of history's most widely read and heartbreaking documents of the Holocaust.

06-12.title: Adriana Lima
06-12.description: Brazilian supermodel who became one of Victoria's Secret's most iconic Angels and one of the world's highest-paid models over a celebrated twenty-year career.

06-12.title: Nelson Mandela Sentenced to Life Imprisonment
06-12.description: Nelson Mandela was sentenced to life in prison at the Rivonia Trial for his anti-apartheid activism, beginning 27 years of imprisonment before emerging to lead South Africa.

06-12.title: Medgar Evers Assassinated
06-12.description: Civil rights leader Medgar Evers was shot dead in his driveway in Jackson, Mississippi, his murder galvanizing the civil rights movement and prompting President Kennedy to call for federal civil rights legislation.

06-12.title: The Joshua Tree — U2
06-12.description: U2's landmark album was released to enormous acclaim and commercial success, featuring Where the Streets Have No Name and I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For, and won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

06-12.title: The Karate Kid
06-12.description: John G. Avildsen's inspirational underdog story of a New Jersey teenager trained by the wise Mr. Miyagi became one of the defining films of 1984 and spawned a beloved franchise.

06-13.title: Tupac Shakur
06-13.description: East Harlem-born rapper whose politically charged lyrics and charismatic intensity made him one of the most influential and revered artists in hip-hop history.

06-13.title: W. B. Yeats
06-13.description: Irish poet and playwright whose mystical, symbolist verse — from The Second Coming to The Lake Isle of Innisfree — won him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1923.

06-13.title: Chris Evans
06-13.description: American actor who embodied the noble spirit of Marvel's Captain America across over a decade of superhero films, becoming one of the defining faces of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

06-13.title: Pentagon Papers Published
06-13.description: The New York Times began publishing the leaked Pentagon Papers, revealing that the US government had systematically deceived the public about the scope and purpose of the Vietnam War.

06-13.title: Edict of Milan Published
06-13.description: Emperor Constantine the Great published the Edict of Milan granting religious tolerance throughout the Roman Empire, fundamentally transforming the relationship between the state and Christianity.

06-13.title: Let It Be — The Beatles
06-13.description: The Beatles' final studio album reached number one in the US charts, its title track and the elegiac The Long and Winding Road serving as a bittersweet farewell to the greatest band in history.

06-13.title: Man of Steel
06-13.description: Zack Snyder's epic reimagining of Superman's origin story launched the DC Extended Universe with Henry Cavill's brooding portrayal of the last son of Krypton.

06-14.title: Che Guevara
06-14.description: Argentine Marxist revolutionary whose role in the Cuban Revolution made his beret-clad portrait the most reproduced image in the history of photography.

06-14.title: Harriet Beecher Stowe
06-14.description: American abolitionist author whose novel Uncle Tom's Cabin exposed the horrors of slavery to a vast Northern readership and inflamed tensions that helped ignite the Civil War.

06-14.title: Donald Trump
06-14.description: Real estate mogul turned reality television star who became the 45th and later 47th President of the United States, one of the most polarizing figures in modern American politics.

06-14.title: US Flag Adopted
06-14.description: The Second Continental Congress passed the Flag Resolution adopting the Stars and Stripes as the official flag of the United States of America.

06-14.title: US Army Founded
06-14.description: The Continental Congress established the Continental Army, the precursor to the United States Army, placing George Washington in supreme command the following day.

06-14.title: Nevermind — Nirvana
06-14.description: Though released in September, Nirvana's explosion into the mainstream was propelled by Smells Like Teen Spirit, which premiered in June 1991, single-handedly launching the grunge era.

06-14.title: Midnight Cowboy
06-14.description: John Schlesinger's gritty, Oscar-winning portrait of two drifters surviving on the margins of New York City remains the only X-rated film ever to win the Academy Award for Best Picture.

06-15.title: Edvard Grieg
06-15.description: Norwegian composer whose Peer Gynt Suites and Piano Concerto in A minor drew on Norwegian folk music to create some of the most beloved Romantic-era orchestral pieces ever written.

06-15.title: Ice Cube
06-15.description: South Central Los Angeles rapper and actor whose incendiary verses on N.W.A's Straight Outta Compton and his subsequent solo career made him one of rap's most formidable voices.

06-15.title: Courteney Cox
06-15.description: American actress who became a household name through her decade-long portrayal of the fiercely competitive Monica Geller on the landmark sitcom Friends.

06-15.title: Magna Carta Sealed
06-15.description: King John of England affixed his seal to Magna Carta at Runnymede, establishing for the first time that the king was subject to the rule of law and laying the cornerstone of modern constitutional democracy.

06-15.title: First Nonstop Transatlantic Flight
06-15.description: Aviators John Alcock and Arthur Brown completed the first ever nonstop transatlantic flight, crash-landing their modified Vickers Vimy biplane in a bog in County Galway, Ireland.

06-15.title: Bleach — Nirvana
06-15.description: Nirvana's low-budget debut album was recorded for just $606 and released on Sub Pop Records, an early raw glimpse of the grunge sound that would soon detonate across popular music.

06-15.title: Batman Begins
06-15.description: Christopher Nolan reinvented the superhero film with this psychologically grounded origin story of Bruce Wayne, launching the Dark Knight trilogy and transforming blockbuster cinema.

06-16.title: Adam Smith
06-16.description: Scottish philosopher and father of modern economics whose 1776 masterwork The Wealth of Nations introduced the concept of the invisible hand and laid the intellectual foundations of capitalism.

06-16.title: Geronimo
06-16.description: Apache leader and military strategist who led fierce resistance against the US and Mexican governments for decades, becoming the most famous Native American warrior of the 19th century.

06-16.title: Katharine Graham
06-16.description: Publisher of the Washington Post who made the brave decision to print both the Pentagon Papers and the Watergate stories, changing American journalism and ultimately ending a presidency.

06-16.title: Valentina Tereshkova Becomes First Woman in Space
06-16.description: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova launched aboard Vostok 6 to become the first woman to travel in space, orbiting Earth 48 times over three days.

06-16.title: IBM Founded
06-16.description: The Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company was established in New York, the company that would be reorganized and renamed IBM in 1924 to become the world's most influential technology firm.

06-16.title: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust — David Bowie
06-16.description: David Bowie released his glam-rock concept album about an androgynous alien rock star, featuring Starman and Suffragette City, a record that changed what it was possible for pop music to be.

06-16.title: Grease
06-16.description: John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John's chemistry ignited this musical phenomenon set in a 1950s high school, which became the highest-grossing musical film of all time upon its June 16 wide release.

06-17.title: Barry Manilow
06-17.description: American singer-songwriter and producer who recorded some of the most successful soft rock and pop songs of the 1970s, including Mandy and Copacabana, selling over 80 million records worldwide.

06-17.title: Venus Williams
06-17.description: American tennis champion who won seven Grand Slam singles titles and helped transform women's tennis into a global spectacle alongside her sister Serena.

06-17.title: Igor Stravinsky
06-17.description: Russian-born composer whose radical Rite of Spring caused a riot at its 1913 premiere and whose career-long reinventions across neoclassicism and serialism made him the most influential composer of the 20th century.

06-17.title: Watergate Burglary
06-17.description: Five burglars were arrested inside the Democratic National Committee headquarters at the Watergate complex in Washington D.C., setting in motion a political scandal that would topple a presidency.

06-17.title: Statue of Liberty Arrives in New York
06-17.description: France's extraordinary gift arrived in New York Harbor packed in 214 crates, awaiting assembly on Bedloe's Island to become one of the world's most enduring symbols of freedom.

06-17.title: The Queen Is Dead — The Smiths
06-17.description: The Smiths released what many consider the greatest British album of the 1980s, Morrissey's sardonic wit matched perfectly against Johnny Marr's shimmering guitar work on the title track and There Is a Light.

06-17.title: The Truman Show
06-17.description: Peter Weir's eerily prescient film starring Jim Carrey as a man who doesn't know his entire life is a live television show anticipated the reality TV era and raised profound questions about authenticity.

06-18.title: Paul McCartney
06-18.description: Co-founder of the Beatles and one of the most successful composers in history, whose melodic genius produced Yesterday, Hey Jude, and a catalog of songs that have never left the airwaves.

06-18.title: Maria Sharapova
06-18.description: Russian tennis star who won five Grand Slam titles and became one of the most recognizable and marketable athletes in the world during her career.

06-18.title: Richard Madden
06-18.description: Scottish actor who first captivated audiences as the doomed Robb Stark in Game of Thrones before his Golden Globe-winning turn in Bodyguard confirmed him as a leading man.

06-18.title: Battle of Waterloo
06-18.description: Napoleon Bonaparte suffered his final defeat at the hands of the Duke of Wellington and Prussian forces near Brussels, ending two decades of French imperial conquest.

06-18.title: Sally Ride Becomes First American Woman in Space
06-18.description: Sally Ride launched aboard Space Shuttle Challenger to become the first American woman in space, inspiring generations of young women to pursue science and exploration.

06-18.title: Hunky Dory — David Bowie
06-18.description: Bowie's fourth album introduced the world to Changes and Life on Mars, a bold artistic leap that established him as one of rock's most visionary songwriters and stylistic chameleons.

06-18.title: Toy Story 3
06-18.description: Pixar's emotionally devastating conclusion to Andy's childhood story became the highest-grossing film of 2010 and earned near-universal praise for reducing audiences of all ages to tears.

06-19.title: Lou Gehrig
06-19.description: New York Yankees first baseman known as the Iron Horse who played 2,130 consecutive games and delivered one of sports history's most poignant farewell speeches upon learning he had ALS.

06-19.title: Zoe Saldana
06-19.description: American actress who has appeared in three of the highest-grossing films of all time — Avatar, Avengers: Infinity War, and Avengers: Endgame — making her the most financially successful actress in box office history.

06-19.title: Salman Rushdie
06-19.description: British-Indian novelist whose Midnight's Children won the Booker Prize and whose novel The Satanic Verses prompted a fatwa from Ayatollah Khomeini that forced him into years of hiding.

06-19.title: Juneteenth: End of Slavery in Texas
06-19.description: Union soldiers arrived in Galveston, Texas to announce that enslaved people were free, more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation, marking the true end of slavery in the United States.

06-19.title: First Father's Day Celebrated
06-19.description: The first Father's Day was celebrated in Spokane, Washington, organized by Sonora Smart Dodd to honor her Civil War veteran father who raised six children alone after his wife's death.

06-19.title: All You Need Is Love — The Beatles
06-19.description: The Beatles performed this peace anthem live before an estimated 400 million viewers in the world's first global satellite television broadcast, Our World, making it the ultimate Summer of Love declaration.

06-19.title: Kramer vs. Kramer
06-19.description: Robert Benton's tender and wrenching drama starring Dustin Hoffman and Meryl Streep in a custody battle swept the Oscars and changed how Hollywood portrayed divorce and parenthood.

06-20.title: Brian Wilson
06-20.description: The Beach Boys' visionary composer and arranger whose ambitious 1966 album Pet Sounds and the single Good Vibrations pushed the boundaries of pop music and directly inspired the Beatles' Sgt. Pepper.

06-20.title: Nicole Kidman
06-20.description: Australian-American actress who won the Academy Award for Best Actress for The Hours and delivered haunting performances in Moulin Rouge! and Eyes Wide Shut that defined early 2000s cinema.

06-20.title: Lionel Richie
06-20.description: American singer-songwriter who authored some of the most recognizable pop melodies of the 1980s including Hello, All Night Long, and Say You Say Me, selling over 100 million records worldwide.

06-20.title: Tennis Court Oath
06-20.description: French Third Estate deputies locked out of their meeting hall gathered on a nearby tennis court and swore not to disperse until France had a new constitution, a pivotal moment sparking the French Revolution.

06-20.title: Watergate White House Tape Gap Discovered
06-20.description: An 18.5-minute gap was discovered in a key White House tape recording of Nixon's conversations with aides, a mysterious erasure that deepened the Watergate scandal and ultimately contributed to Nixon's resignation.

06-20.title: HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I — Michael Jackson
06-20.description: Michael Jackson's double album of greatest hits and new material debuted at number one in 20 countries and included the powerful new single Scream, a duet with his sister Janet.

06-20.title: Jaws
06-20.description: Steven Spielberg's terrifying shark thriller invented the summer blockbuster and made an entire generation afraid to go back in the water, becoming the highest-grossing film in history upon its release.

06-21.title: Jean-Paul Sartre
06-21.description: French philosopher, playwright, and novelist whose concept of existentialism — captured in Being and Nothingness and the play No Exit — made him one of the most influential thinkers of the 20th century.

06-21.title: Chris Pratt
06-21.description: American actor who transformed from lovable sitcom slacker Andy Dwyer in Parks and Recreation to a Hollywood leading man as Star-Lord in Guardians of the Galaxy and Owen in the Jurassic World franchise.

06-21.title: Jane Russell
06-21.description: Hollywood actress and one of the leading sex symbols of the 1940s and 1950s, who starred alongside Marilyn Monroe in the classic musical comedy Gentlemen Prefer Blondes.

06-21.title: Oda Nobunaga Dies
06-21.description: The most powerful Japanese warlord of his era, Oda Nobunaga, was betrayed by his own general Akechi Mitsuhide and forced to commit ritual suicide, ending his mission to unify Japan.

06-21.title: Summer Solstice
06-21.description: The summer solstice marks the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, a celestial event celebrated by ancient cultures from Stonehenge to Scandinavia for thousands of years.

06-21.title: Achtung Baby — U2
06-21.description: U2 announced their bold reinvention by recording this dark, industrial-inflected album in Berlin, with the lead single The Fly subverting Bono's earnest rock-star persona and catapulting the band into the 1990s.

06-21.title: Toy Story 4
06-21.description: Pixar's fourth installment brought Woody and Buzz back for a bittersweet road trip adventure that surprised critics and audiences with its mature emotional resonance, winning the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.

06-22.title: Billy Wilder
06-22.description: Austrian-American filmmaker whose razor-sharp wit produced enduring Hollywood classics including Some Like It Hot, Sunset Boulevard, Double Indemnity, and The Apartment.

06-22.title: Cyndi Lauper
06-22.description: Flamboyant New Wave pop icon whose 1983 debut album She's So Unusual spawned four Top 5 hits including Girls Just Want to Have Fun and Time After Time, and whose colorful style defined the 1980s.

06-22.title: Meryl Streep
06-22.description: American actress widely regarded as the greatest living film actress, with a record 21 Academy Award nominations and three wins for Kramer vs. Kramer, Sophie's Choice, and The Iron Lady.

06-22.title: Galileo Recants Heliocentrism
06-22.description: The Inquisition forced Galileo Galilei to recant his scientific finding that Earth orbits the Sun, placing the astronomer under house arrest for the remainder of his life in one of history's most shameful episodes of censorship.

06-22.title: Maradona's Hand of God Goal
06-22.description: Diego Maradona scored his infamous Hand of God goal against England in the World Cup quarter-final with his fist, then moments later scored the Goal of the Century with his feet, in a single match that defined footballing mythology.

06-22.title: She's So Unusual — Cyndi Lauper
06-22.description: Cyndi Lauper's debut album was released and became a pop culture landmark, producing four Top 5 singles and winning Lauper the Grammy Award for Best New Artist.

06-22.title: The Fast and the Furious
06-22.description: Rob Cohen's adrenaline-fueled street-racing thriller launched one of the most commercially successful film franchises in history, making instant stars of Vin Diesel and Paul Walker.

06-23.title: Alan Turing
06-23.description: British mathematician and pioneer of computer science whose Enigma code-breaking at Bletchley Park helped win World War II and whose theoretical work laid the foundation for the modern computer.

06-23.title: Zinedine Zidane
06-23.description: French football maestro widely regarded as one of the greatest players of all time, who guided France to the 1998 World Cup and the 2000 European Championship with transcendent technical skill.

06-23.title: Frances McDormand
06-23.description: American actress who won three Academy Awards for Best Actress for Fargo, Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri, and Nomadland, cementing her reputation as one of cinema's finest character actors.

06-23.title: Battle of Bannockburn
06-23.description: Robert the Bruce led his Scottish army to a decisive victory over English forces at Bannockburn, securing Scottish independence and establishing him firmly as King Robert I of Scotland.

06-23.title: Brexit Referendum
06-23.description: The United Kingdom voted 51.9% to 48.1% to leave the European Union in a historic referendum that shocked world markets, reshaped British politics, and took effect in 2020.

06-23.title: Coming Home — Leon Bridges
06-23.description: Leon Bridges released his debut album of retro-soul that sounded like a lost Sam Cooke recording, earning him a Grammy Award for Best Traditional R&B Performance and an immediate place in music history.

06-23.title: When Harry Met Sally
06-23.description: Rob Reiner's beloved romantic comedy starring Meg Ryan and Billy Crystal posed the enduring question of whether men and women can ever be just friends, and featured the diner scene that became one of cinema's greatest comic moments.

06-24.title: Lionel Messi
06-24.description: Argentine footballer who has won eight Ballon d'Or awards and guided his nation to the 2021 Copa América and the 2022 FIFA World Cup, making him the undisputed greatest player in the history of the sport.

06-24.title: Jack Dempsey
06-24.description: Heavyweight boxing champion from 1919 to 1926 whose aggressive fighting style and enormous popularity helped transform boxing into a major American spectator sport.

06-24.title: Mick Fleetwood
06-24.description: British drummer and co-founder of Fleetwood Mac, who steered the band through numerous lineup changes to the era-defining Rumours album, one of the best-selling records in history.

06-24.title: Napoleon Invades Russia
06-24.description: Napoleon Bonaparte led his Grande Armée of 600,000 troops across the Niemen River into Russia, beginning a catastrophic campaign that would result in the destruction of his army and the collapse of his empire.

06-24.title: Julia Gillard Becomes Australia's First Female Prime Minister
06-24.description: Julia Gillard was sworn in as Australia's 27th Prime Minister, making history as the first woman to hold the nation's highest political office.

06-24.title: Rumours — Fleetwood Mac
06-24.description: Fleetwood Mac's masterpiece of tension and heartbreak became one of the best-selling albums in history, spending 31 weeks at number one and featuring Go Your Own Way, The Chain, and Dreams.

06-24.title: The Dark Knight Rises
06-24.description: Christopher Nolan brought his acclaimed Batman trilogy to a thunderous conclusion with Tom Hardy's terrifying Bane and a climax that had audiences gripping their armrests.

06-25.title: George Orwell
06-25.description: British author whose works Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four remain the most powerful literary warnings against totalitarianism ever written, coining concepts that permeate our political vocabulary.

06-25.title: George Michael
06-25.description: British singer-songwriter who went from Wham! teen idol to one of the most artistically accomplished solo artists of his generation with Faith and Listen Without Prejudice Vol. 1.

06-25.title: Sonia Sotomayor
06-25.description: The first Hispanic and third female Justice of the United States Supreme Court, appointed by President Obama in 2009, who grew up in a Bronx housing project and became a symbol of American possibility.

06-25.title: Battle of the Little Bighorn
06-25.description: Lakota and Cheyenne warriors led by Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse annihilated Lieutenant Colonel George Custer's 7th Cavalry at the Little Bighorn River in the most famous Native American victory over US forces.

06-25.title: Korean War Begins
06-25.description: North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel in a surprise invasion of South Korea, drawing in the United States and United Nations in a brutal three-year conflict that ended in an armistice rather than a peace treaty.

06-25.title: Reasonable Doubt — Jay-Z
06-25.description: Jay-Z released his debut album on his own Roc-A-Fella Records label, a raw and vivid portrait of hustling in Brooklyn that critics now recognize as one of the greatest hip-hop albums ever made.

06-25.title: It Happened One Night
06-25.description: Frank Capra's screwball romantic comedy with Clark Gable and Claudette Colbert became the first film to win all five major Academy Awards and defined the genre for decades.

06-26.title: Lord Kelvin
06-26.description: Scottish physicist William Thomson who formulated the second law of thermodynamics and proposed the absolute temperature scale that bears his name, revolutionizing 19th-century physics.

06-26.title: Pearl S. Buck
06-26.description: American novelist who grew up in China and won the Nobel Prize in Literature for her vivid portrayal of Chinese rural life in The Good Earth, one of the best-selling novels of the 20th century.

06-26.title: Abner Doubleday
06-26.description: Union Army general who is often credited in American folklore with inventing the game of baseball, though historians dispute the claim, and who notably ordered the first shots in defense of Fort Sumter.

06-26.title: United Nations Charter Signed
06-26.description: Representatives of 50 nations signed the United Nations Charter in San Francisco, establishing the international organization created to prevent another world war and promote peace, security, and human rights.

06-26.title: Supreme Court Rules Same-Sex Marriage Legal
06-26.description: In the landmark Obergefell v. Hodges ruling, the US Supreme Court held that the Constitution guarantees same-sex couples the right to marry, a decision celebrated across the nation with rainbow-lit landmarks.

06-26.title: "I ♥ NY" Jingle — Steve Karmen
06-26.description: The iconic I Love New York advertising jingle debuted in 1977 as part of a campaign to revive a bankrupt city, and its simple four-note melody became one of the most recognizable tunes ever written.

06-26.title: The Gold Rush
06-26.description: Charlie Chaplin's Klondike comedy, which premiered on June 26, blended slapstick genius with genuine pathos in the bread-roll ballet scene, cementing Chaplin as cinema's greatest comic artist.

06-27.title: Helen Keller
06-27.description: American author and activist who, despite becoming deaf and blind at 19 months old, graduated from Radcliffe College and became one of history's most inspiring advocates for disability rights.

06-27.title: Paul Laurence Dunbar
06-27.description: American poet who was the first African American to gain international recognition as a writer, his dialect poetry and standard English verse capturing the Black American experience with grace and power.

06-27.title: Ross Perot
06-27.description: American billionaire businessman and independent presidential candidate who captured nearly 19% of the popular vote in 1992, one of the most successful third-party runs in modern American political history.

06-27.title: Joseph Smith Killed
06-27.description: Joseph Smith, founder of the Latter Day Saint movement, was killed by a mob at the Carthage jail in Illinois, making him a martyr whose death accelerated rather than ended the movement he started.

06-27.title: First Nuclear Power Plant Opens
06-27.description: The Soviet Union opened the Obninsk Nuclear Power Plant, the world's first nuclear power station to generate electricity for a power grid, opening the nuclear age for civilian energy.

06-27.title: Cosmic Thing — B-52s
06-27.description: The B-52s released their comeback album featuring Love Shack and Roam, becoming the band's best-selling record and one of the most joyous albums of the late 1980s.

06-27.title: WALL-E
06-27.description: Pixar's nearly wordless masterpiece about a lonely trash-compacting robot on a desolate future Earth captivated audiences and critics alike, winning the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.

06-28.title: Henry VIII
06-28.description: The most iconic English monarch, whose six marriages, break from Rome to establish the Church of England, and colossal appetites in all things made him a figure of enduring fascination.

06-28.title: Elon Musk
06-28.description: South African-born entrepreneur who founded SpaceX to make humanity multi-planetary, led Tesla's electric vehicle revolution, and acquired Twitter in 2022, reshaping three industries in two decades.

06-28.title: Mel Brooks
06-28.description: American filmmaker and comedian whose satirical masterpieces Blazing Saddles and Young Frankenstein remain two of the funniest films ever made, and whose career as writer, director, and performer spans seven decades.

06-28.title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
06-28.description: Austro-Hungarian heir Archduke Franz Ferdinand was shot dead in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip, setting off a chain of alliances and ultimatums that plunged the world into the catastrophe of World War I.

06-28.title: Stonewall Inn Riots
06-28.description: Patrons of the Stonewall Inn in Greenwich Village fought back against a police raid, sparking six nights of protests that launched the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement and gave rise to Pride marches worldwide.

06-28.title: The Bends — Radiohead
06-28.description: Radiohead's second album announced their arrival as one of rock's most distinctive voices, with Fake Plastic Trees and High and Dry establishing Thom Yorke's plaintive alienation as the emotional signature of a generation.

06-28.title: Rocky
06-28.description: Sylvester Stallone's underdog boxing drama, which he wrote in three days, won three Academy Awards including Best Picture and launched one of cinema's most enduring franchises.

06-29.title: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
06-29.description: French aviator and author whose novella The Little Prince has become the most translated French-language book in history and one of the most beloved children's stories ever written.

06-29.title: Gary Busey
06-29.description: American actor who earned an Academy Award nomination for his electrifying portrayal of rock legend Buddy Holly in The Buddy Holly Story.

06-29.title: George Washington Goethals
06-29.description: US Army engineer who overcame enormous obstacles of engineering, disease, and logistics to complete the Panama Canal in 1914, connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

06-29.title: Globe Theatre Burns Down
06-29.description: Shakespeare's legendary Globe Theatre was destroyed by fire during a performance of Henry VIII when a stage cannon misfired, burning to the ground in about two hours.

06-29.title: First iPhone Goes on Sale
06-29.description: Apple's original iPhone went on sale to customers queued around the block outside Apple Stores, launching the smartphone revolution that would fundamentally remake modern society.

06-29.title: Slipknot — Slipknot
06-29.description: Iowa's nine-piece masked metal outfit released their self-titled major-label debut, a crushing assault of polyrhythmic chaos that redefined heavy music and launched one of metal's most dedicated cult followings.

06-29.title: The Notebook
06-29.description: Nick Cassavetes' sweeping romance starring Ryan Gosling and Rachel McAdams became one of the defining love stories of the 2000s, turning its two leads into A-list stars.

06-30.title: Michael Phelps
06-30.description: American swimmer who won 23 Olympic gold medals across four Games, the most decorated Olympian in history, whose long torso and wingspan seemed engineered by nature for the pool.

06-30.title: Lena Horne
06-30.description: African American singer, actress, and civil rights activist whose 70-year career broke racial barriers in Hollywood and produced the timeless standards Stormy Weather and The Lady Is a Tramp.

06-30.title: Mike Tyson
06-30.description: Brooklyn-born heavyweight boxing champion who became the youngest world heavyweight title holder in history at age 20 and whose ferocious punching power made him the most feared fighter of his era.

06-30.title: Tunguska Event
06-30.description: A massive asteroid or comet exploded over a remote Siberian forest near the Tunguska River, releasing energy 1,000 times greater than the Hiroshima bomb and flattening 2,000 square kilometers of trees.

06-30.title: Einstein Publishes Special Relativity
06-30.description: Albert Einstein submitted his paper On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies for publication, introducing the special theory of relativity and the concept that the speed of light is constant for all observers.

06-30.title: Back in Black — AC/DC
06-30.description: AC/DC's thunderous tribute to their late singer Bon Scott became the second best-selling album in history with an estimated 50 million copies sold, its opening riff among the most recognizable in rock.

06-30.title: Superman
06-30.description: Richard Donner's epic superhero film with Christopher Reeve made audiences believe a man could fly and established the template for the modern superhero blockbuster.
